deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Take a 2-sheeted covering Φ = ⨿_{i∈I} Φ_i → I with |I| = 3 and |Φ_i| = 2. The combinatorial 3-cube C, and dually the octahedron O (the 3-dimensional cross-polytope), are described by partial sections of Φ → I. These are the nonempty subsets A ⊂ Φ that map injectively to I.
- The k-element partial sections give O_{k-1}: vertices = Φ, edges = 2-element sections, triangles = full sections.
- The same sets index the faces of C in reverse order: C_2 = Φ, C_1 = edges, C_0 = full sections.
- Incidence is inclusion, or reverse inclusion for C.
- The canonical involution a acts as the identity on I and swaps the two points of each Φ_i. It is the antipodal map on both C and O.

This page. Grothendieck passes to the quotient by {1, a}. He first wrote 'projectif', then crossed it out and replaced it by 'grand'. He sets C̃_i = C_i/{1,a} and Õ_i = O_i/{1,a}, with the induced incidence; in modern terms these are the hemi-cube and the hemi-octahedron.
- The hemi-octahedron has 3 vertices, 6 edges and 4 faces.
- He identifies it with the cell decomposition of the real projective plane by three lines in general position, indexed by I.
- The line D_i is made of two projective edges. These are the images of the four ordinary edges A ∈ P_2(Φ) with A ↪ I∖{i}. This is the square equator of the octahedron orthogonal to the i-axis, which becomes a projective line with 2 vertices and 2 edges.

He then notes that C (or O) cannot be recovered from C̃ (or Õ) up to isomorphism, because the automorphism groups differ. Aut(C) is the hyperoctahedral group of order 48, Aut(C̃) is S_4 of order 24, and a is a nontrivial central element that maps to the identity. So C ↦ C̃ is neither fully faithful nor faithful.

Next page. He repairs this with oriented cubes and octahedra: the rotation group ≅ S_4 maps isomorphically onto Aut(C̃). He gives a canonical description of the orientation torsor as (∧_i Φ_i) ∧ or(I), and recovers C from C̃ as the canonical orientation double cover.

Purpose. This is the base case, 'arrangements of 3 pseudo-lines', of a combinatorial study of pseudo-line arrangements in RP^2. These are viewed as quotients of centrally symmetric cell decompositions of S^2, i.e. zonotope/oriented-matroid-like structures.
errors: No mathematical errors. The counts (3,6,4) for the hemi-octahedron and the implied (4,6,3) for the hemi-cube are correct, and Euler characteristic 1 = χ(RP^2) is consistent. The description of each line D_i as 2 projective edges coming from 4 ordinary edges is correct. The claim that the automorphism groups differ (48 vs 24) is correct.

ideas.what: Face poset of the cube/cross-polytope as partial sections of a double cover Φ→I, ordered by inclusion
ideas.modern_name: Cross-polytope face lattice as sign vectors / covectors of the coordinate oriented matroid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; sign-vector formalism of oriented matroids (Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence 1978)

ideas.what: Quotient of cube/octahedron by the antipodal map ('grand cube', 'grand octaèdre')
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses combinatorial regular polyhedra, but whether it covers hemi-polyhedra specifically is unsure

ideas.what: Hemi-octahedron = cell decomposition of RP^2 by three lines in general position; each line = image of an equatorial square
ideas.modern_name: Simple arrangement of 3 (pseudo)lines in RP^2 / rank-3 coordinate oriented matroid; antipodal quotient of a central sphere arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Levi 1926; Grünbaum, Goodman–Pollack; Folkman–Lawrence topological representation)

ideas.what: The functor C ↦ C̃ is not faithful (the antipode is killed); Aut drops from order 48 to 24
ideas.modern_name: Hyperoctahedral group B_3 = S_4 × Z/2 → S_4, with kernel the central antipode

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, functorial re-derivation of classical facts: the hemi-cube and hemi-octahedron, three lines in RP^2, and the 48 → 24 automorphism comparison. It sets up the base case of his pseudo-line study. The only idiosyncratic features are the terminology 'grand' replacing 'projectif' and the functorial framing; the latter pays off on the next page with the orientation torsor. There is nothing new for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the quotient is 'par ±' and the inserted words 'grands (ou' belong to '(grands (ou) cubes combinatoires projectifs) C̃'. Likewise '(grands (ou) comb. projectifs) Õ'. So the reading is 'Passant au quotient par ±, on trouve les cubes combinatoires (grands ou projectifs) C̃, et d'octaèdres comb. (grands ou projectifs) Õ, associés à a'.
Formula (4) is likely C̃_i = C_i/{1,a} and Õ_i = O_i/{1,a}; the subscript on C and O is hard to read in the image.
'À isomorphismes près' appears as 'à isom. "grands" canoniques près' (the word 'grands' inserted above), i.e. a phrase about canonical isomorphisms, not 'à isomorphismes près' plainly.
'en dimension [?] que' should probably read 'en ce sens que' (or 'du fait que'). 'groupes d'automorphismes' has 'd'automorphismes' inserted above the line.
'Le' was corrected to 'L'' in 'L'octaèdre grand', and 'projectif' is crossed out with 'grand' written above.
The (A ↪ I∖{i}) closing parenthesis/sentence ends with 'A ↪ I∖{i}.'
